population.title: Cell Population Model
population.warnCollateral: {pct}% of healthy cells cross the lysis threshold, reduce field or tune frequency.
population.okWindow: {pct}% of target cells lysed · 0% healthy collateral. Selectivity window is effective.
population.tipPopSize: Population Size N N=100: fast, coarse histogram — quick parameter scans N=300: balanced default, smooth histogram N=1000: high-fidelity — ideal for final protocol analysis Larger N reduces statistical noise on each percentage badge (shown as ±SE).
population.tipRVariance: Radius Variance σ_R / R Gaussian spread of cell radius as % of mean R. Models natural cell-to-cell size heterogeneity. Mammalian: ~10% · Bacteria: ~20% · Virus: ~30% Vm ∝ R, so larger cells sit closer to the lysis threshold. Sampled range clamped to [0.4·R₀, 2.0·R₀].
population.tipVThVariance: Lysis Threshold Variance σ_{Vth} / V_th Gaussian spread of the per-cell lysis threshold voltage. Models variation in membrane composition, cholesterol:phospholipid ratio, cell-cycle phase, and pre-existing membrane tension. Literature (Weaver & Chizmadzhev 1996): CV ≈ 20-35% in isogenic mammalian populations. Default 20% is conservative; 25-30% is more realistic for heterogeneous tissue. Higher variance widens the DR distribution and broadens the lysis transition zone, giving a more realistic prediction of population-level response. Sampled range clamped to [0.5·Vth₀, 2.0·Vth₀].
population.tipResample: ⟳ Resample Generate a new random population draw. R, σ_i, and V_th are sampled independently per cell (Box-Muller Gaussian): σ_R = R₀ × R_variance% σ(σ_i) = σ_i × uncertainty (mammalian 20% · bacteria 35% · virus 45%) σ(V_th) = V_th × V_th_variance% (Weaver & Chizmadzhev 1996) Note: resonant frequency scaling for rod-shaped bacteria (E. coli) assumes spherical geometry (f ∝ 1/R). Rod aspect ratio effects on acoustic modes are not modelled.
population.tipExport: ↓ Export CSV Download all sampled DR values with full experiment metadata. Columns: cell_type · sample_index · DR Metadata includes R variance, V_th variance, σ_i uncertainty, field parameters, and Population Window Score.
population.tipTargetCard: Target Population: {label} Outcome distribution at current field settings. R, σ_i, and V_th sampled from Gaussian distributions. σ_i uncertainty: ±{uncPct}% DR = Vm(R, σ_i, f, E) × f_pulse(τ, t_p) / V_th Each percentage shows ±SE (binomial standard error): SE = √(p·(1−p)/N) × 100.
population.tipHealthyCard: Healthy Population: {label} Outcome distribution under the same shared field. Goal: 0% Lysed · low Rev-EP · high Stable fraction. σ_i uncertainty: ±{uncPct}% Each percentage shows ±SE (binomial standard error): SE = √(p·(1−p)/N) × 100.
population.tipLysedTarget: Target Lysed: {pct}% ±{se}% Fraction with DR ≥ 1.0, irreversible membrane disruption. ±{se}% is the binomial standard error at current N. Goal: maximise this fraction.
population.tipRevEpTarget: Target Rev-EP: {pct}% ±{se}% DR 0.50-1.0, reversible electroporation zone. Membrane transiently permeabilised; may recover with fewer pulses or lower duty cycle.
population.tipNourTarget: Target Nourishing: {pct}% ±{se}% DR 0.08-0.50, sub-EP Schwan coupling. Membrane partially stressed; cell is intact and may show mechanotransduction responses.
population.tipLysedHealthy: Healthy Lysed: {pct}% ±{se}% ⚠ Collateral damage — DR ≥ 1.0. Keep at 0%. Reduce field, increase frequency, or shorten pulse width.
population.tipRevEpHealthy: Healthy Rev-EP: {pct}% ±{se}% DR 0.50-1.0, reversible EP zone. Reversible at low duty cycle; monitor for cumulative pore-formation with repeated pulse trains.
population.tipNourHealthy: Healthy Nourishing: {pct}% ±{se}% DR 0.08-0.50, sub-lytic Schwan coupling. Low-level membrane activity. Generally safe; may support tissue nourishing responses.
population.tipWindowScore: Population Window Score WS = (% Target Lysed / 100) × (1 − % Healthy Lysed / 100) Current: WS = {score} — {verdict} Target lysed: {pctT}% Healthy lysed: {pctH}% Interpretation: ≥ 0.50 Effective window, protocol is viable 0.20-0.49 Marginal window, adjust field or frequency < 0.20 Poor window, protocol needs redesign WS = 1.0: all target cells lysed, zero healthy collateral (ideal). WS = 0.0: no target lysis or complete healthy destruction.
population.tipChart: Population DR Histogram Monte Carlo disruption ratio distribution (Box-Muller Gaussian sampling). Red = Target cells · Cyan = Healthy cells Threshold lines: 50%: Rev-EP onset 85%: Lysis countdown armed 100%: Lysis threshold Ideal protocol: target distribution entirely above 100% · healthy distribution entirely below 50%. Use Fraction mode for shape comparison independent of N.
population.tipNormalize: Histogram Y-Axis Mode Count: raw cell count per DR bin Fraction: proportion of population per bin (0-1, shown as %) Fraction mode makes distribution shape directly comparable across different N values, and is the standard representation for population-level analysis in published protocols.
population.tipNPill100: N=100 Fast — coarse histogram. Binomial SE is large (~5% at p=0.5). Best for rapid parameter scans.
population.tipNPill300: N=300 Balanced default: smooth histogram. Binomial SE ~3% at p=0.5.
population.tipNPill1000: N=1000 High-fidelity — slow sampling. Binomial SE ~1.6% at p=0.5. Ideal for final protocol analysis and publication.
population.tipMeanDr: Mean DR ± σ DR = Vm(R, σ_i, f, E) × f_pulse / V_th Mean: {mean} · σ (population spread): {std} σ_i uncertainty ±{uncPct}% modelled in each sample. Note: σ here is the population standard deviation of DR, not the SE of the mean.

population.csvTarget: Target:  {label} · R={radius} {um} · N={n} · σ_i ±{uncPct}% · R ±{rPct}% · V_th ±{vthPct}%
